result_semantic_payload.summary: The device contains two small record sets plus a README: /shop/refunds.csv (2 refund rows) and /finance/payouts.log (3 payout rows). They join on refund_id and amount: RF-9001 (1200) and RF-9002 (3400) appear in both, with identical amounts. RF-9003 (8800) appears only in payouts.log with no matching row in refunds.csv, so it is an orphan payout not supported by any shop refund record. All three payouts go to the same card, masked as *7712. The evidence does NOT identify any individual as the payout recipient: neither refunds.csv (customers customerA, customerB, tied to refund_ids only) nor payouts.log (destination is a masked card number) names a cardholder, and the README explicitly states the card holder is not identified in either system. Therefore no individual can be attributed as the payout recipient on this evidence; a shared payout card across three refunds is a weak indicator at best and cannot be elevated to a single-perpetrator conclusion.

claim_candidates.text: refunds.csv contains exactly two refund records: RF-9001 (order ORD-55101, customer customerA, amount 1200) and RF-9002 (order ORD-55102, customer customerB, amount 3400).

payouts.log contains exactly three payout records dated 2024-09-01, 2024-09-02 and 2024-09-03, for refund_ids RF-9001 (1200), RF-9002 (3400) and RF-9003 (8800), all marked 'ok' and all sent to card *7712.

RF-9001 and RF-9002 join cleanly between the shop refund table and the finance payout log on both refund_id and amount (1200 and 3400 respectively), so those two refunds are corroborated by a corresponding payout.
RF-9003 (amount 8800) appears in payouts.log but has no corresponding row in refunds.csv; it is an orphan payout with no supporting shop refund record on this device.
All three payouts in payouts.log are directed to the same masked card *7712; the log records only the card's last four digits, not a cardholder name.

No individual can be attributed as the payout recipient on the basis of this evidence: the refund table's customer field (customerA, customerB) is tied to refund_ids, not to payout destinations, and the payout log identifies only a masked card number whose holder is not named in either file.

The README.txt on the device explicitly states that payouts all land on the same card, that RF-9003 has no row in the refund table, and that the card holder is not identified in either system — i.e., the source material itself flags that asserting a single perpetrator from the shared payout card would exceed the evidence.
The common card *7712 across three refund payouts is at most a weak correlation hint; it does not establish identity, intent, or authorship, and cannot support a single-perpetrator conclusion.
limitations: No account, identity, or authentication record links card *7712 to any named individual.
No Windows telemetry (event logs, prefetch, amcache, registry) is present in the task to corroborate execution or user activity.
No Windows telemetry (event logs, prefetch, Amcache, registry, USN journal) is present in the task, so no attribution to a user account or executing process is possible.
Payouts.log records only the last four digits of the card (*7712); no cardholder name, PAN, account number, or bank identifier is available.
refunds.csv 'customer' values (customerA, customerB) are tied to refund_ids only and are not shown to be the payout recipients; no field in either file links a customer to a payout destination.
RF-9003 has no row in the refund table on this device; whether it was deleted, never created, or exists on another system cannot be determined from the available evidence.

No file timestamps distinguish authoring/edit times of the two record sets — both were created at the same captured timestamp — so ordering of shop vs. finance activity cannot be inferred beyond the payout dates inside payouts.log.
README.txt is an in-image narrative note rather than an independent forensic artifact; it is used here as corroborating context, not as the primary basis for the join findings.
warnings: The task metadata reports no platform scenario and no registered source scopes, so the 'windows' scope delegation is effectively served by three flat files only.

Attribution of a single individual as payout recipient would overstate the evidence: the shared card *7712 across three refunds is a correlation hint at most, and the README explicitly warns against that leap.
